full_judgment:
2. The petitioner as pre-emptor filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 32 of 1992 against the opposite parties Nos. 1 and 2 as pre-emptees under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The pre-emptees opposite parties entered appearance and took adjournment for filing written objection and ultimately 2 days earlier of the date of ex parte hearing of the case on 21-9-93, filed the written objection on 19-9-93 with the prayer for acceptance of the same. But the Court kept those in the record with an order to put up the same on the date fixed i.e. on 21-9-93 for hearing and order. On 21-9-93 the pre-emptor petitioner filed hajira and the pre-emptees were absent. The case was heard in ex parte on rejection, of the written objection and thereby the Court allowed pre-emption in favour of the pre-emptor petitioner. 

 12. In consideration of. the facts and circumstance of the case and the legal position stated above it is held that if an application under Order IX rule 13 is dismissed for non-appearance of the petitioner, certainly this becomes an appealable order under Order XLIII rule 1(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, but when the dismissal is for non-taking of step regarding deposit of certain postal requisites for no fault of the applicants-petitioners but for the mistake done by the Courts official the same trial court may by invoking the power under section 151 restore the Miscellaneous Case to its file and number upon setting aside the dismissal order to rectify the defects done by the Court's official to do complete justice and thereby to save the parties from further litigation in other provisions of the Code and in such a case the question of limitation is immaterial.
